entry.englishMeaning: progressing as planned toward a goal
entry.coreIdea: A train following the route to its destination.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative planning expression: progress is compared with staying on the correct route toward a destination.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive and reassuring here: the review is progressing as planned.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Confident and matter-of-fact here: the speaker expects the Thursday target to be met.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral and common in everyday and professional planning. It can describe schedules, budgets or goals.

when_to_use: Report that current progress supports reaching a goal, using completed work or other evidence.
when_not_to_use: On track predicts progress toward a goal; on schedule specifically compares progress with planned dates.

advanced_nuance: On track is a judgement based on current progress, not a guarantee. State the evidence and update the assessment if conditions change.
On track can refer to quality, spending or another goal as well as timing. On schedule specifically concerns planned dates.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A train following the route to its destination.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: My savings are on track to cover the course fee by June.
memory_practice.production_task: Use “on track” in your own response: Give an evidence-based update showing that a monthly target is likely to be met.
memory_practice.recall_question: Without looking at the heading, recall the expression meaning “progressing as planned toward a goal”. Then explain it in your own words.
memory_practice.recognition_task: Compare these two statements and choose the accurate form or interpretation. A: “We are on the track to finish.” B: “We are on track to finish.” Explain the difference before checking Mistakes & Differences.

examples.workplace: We are on track to finish the review by Thursday.
examples.another_context: My savings are on track to cover the course fee by June.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Are we still on track to finish by Thursday?
B: Yes. Only the final two sections remain, and both reviewers are available tomorrow.
A: Good. Let me know if anything changes.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: We are on track to finish the review by Thursday.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: progressing as planned toward a goal
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The review is progressing well enough that finishing by Thursday currently looks achievable. The phrase reports the present outlook, not a promise that nothing can go wrong.

mistakes_differences.correction: We are on track to finish.
mistakes_differences.common_mistake: We are on the track to finish.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: On track predicts progress toward a goal; on schedule specifically compares progress with planned dates.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: on track: be on track to + verb; keep + noun on track

semanticReview.finding: Valid examples and exercises preserved; evidence-based dialogue and no-guarantee distinction sharpened.

entry.coreIdea: A progress bar that has not reached 100%.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: State expression meaning that an activity has started but is not yet complete.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: it reports the current stage without implying success, delay or failure.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Factual and status-focused here: “still” emphasizes that the final check continues.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral; natural in everyday updates, workplace reports and system-status messages.

when_to_use: Report that an activity has started and is continuing but is not yet finished.
when_not_to_use: In progress states unfinished status; under way often draws attention to the fact that something has started.

advanced_nuance: In progress gives no percentage or reliable finish time by itself. Provide those details separately if you know them.
Still in progress emphasizes continuation. It can suggest a longer wait than expected in some contexts, but does not by itself prove a delay.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A progress bar that has not reached 100%.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Dinner was still in progress when the guests arrived.
memory_practice.production_task: Use “in progress” in your own response: Write a status message for a review that has started but has no reliable completion time.
memory_practice.recall_question: Without looking at the heading, recall the expression meaning “started but not yet completed”. Then explain it in your own words.
memory_practice.recognition_task: Compare these two statements and choose the accurate form or interpretation. A: “The check is on progress.” B: “The check is in progress.” Explain the difference before checking Mistakes & Differences.

examples.workplace: The final check is still in progress.
examples.another_context: Dinner was still in progress when the guests arrived.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Is the final check complete?
B: Not yet. It is still in progress.
A: Please let me know when the results are ready.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: The final check is still in progress.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The final check has begun and is continuing. Still emphasizes that it has not finished; it does not tell us how much is done or prove that the check is late.

mistakes_differences.important_difference: In progress states unfinished status; under way often draws attention to the fact that something has started.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: in progress: be in progress; work in progress

semanticReview.finding: Valid grammar and examples retained; ongoing status distinguished from percentage, completion and proven delay.

entry.englishMeaning: to be willing or interested in doing something
entry.coreIdea: A raised hand saying count me in.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Informal idiomatic phrase asking whether someone is willing or interested in an activity.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive and inviting here: the walk is offered as an optional shared activity.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Friendly and low-pressure here: the question leaves the listener free to accept or decline.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Informal conversation. “Would you be interested in…” is more suitable for a formal invitation.

when_to_use: Make or answer a friendly, informal invitation to an activity.
when_not_to_use: Be up for expresses willingness; feel up to emphasises sufficient energy.
Informal and friendly; would you be interested in is a more formal invitation.

advanced_nuance: Be up for is informal and friendly; would you be interested in is a more formal way to invite someone.
After be up for, use a noun or an -ing form: up for a walk or up for walking. A willing response does not necessarily confirm the final time or arrangements.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A raised hand saying count me in.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: I would be up for a picnic if the weather stays dry.
memory_practice.production_task: Invite a friend to a short walk after lunch. Respond in one or two natural sentences using the expression, then compare with the pattern after answering.
memory_practice.recall_question: Recall the expression for this meaning without looking: to be willing or interested in doing something. Explain its function in one sentence.
memory_practice.recognition_task: Which option fits the taught meaning and standard construction? A: Would you be up for to walk? B: Would you be up for a walk? Explain your choice, then check the correction and distinction.

examples.scenario: Would you be up for a walk after lunch?
examples.another_setting: I would be up for a picnic if the weather stays dry.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: I would be up for a picnic if the weather stays dry.
B: Great; I will check the forecast tomorrow.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Would you be up for a walk after lunch?
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to be willing or interested in doing something
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker asks whether the listener would like to join a walk after lunch. Be up for expresses willingness or interest in this invitation.

mistakes_differences.correction: Would you be up for a walk?
mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Would you be up for to walk?
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Be up for expresses willingness; feel up to emphasises sufficient energy.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: be up for: be up for + noun/-ing

semanticReview.finding: Valid invitation lesson retained; noun/gerund construction and willingness versus confirmed arrangements clarified.
